title: The Merry Jest of the Remorseful Thief

keywords: a merry jest of a clever thief
full_text:
A witty thief in Baghdad broke into the house of an affluent, stingy merchant who never gave a copper to charity. The thief took an embroidered silk coat, a silver washbasin, and a bag of walnuts.

However, feeling a pang of humorous conscience, the thief left upon the dining table a beautifully handwritten poem:
'I borrowed your coat because winter is cold,
Your basin to wash, and your walnuts of gold;
When the spring flowers blossom and my fortunes arise,
I shall bring back your goods with a pleasant surprise!'

Three months later, the thief returned to the merchant’s garden at night: he returned the silk coat freshly washed and pressed, the silver basin polished like a mirror, and replaced the walnuts with a basket of fresh, sweet Syrian figs and ten gold dinars!

He included a note: 'The loan is repaid with interest; I have opened an honest grocery, and shall never borrow at midnight again!'

The merchant laughed heartily, dropped all charges, and became the former thief’s best customer, proving that good humor can sweeten repentance.
moral: Even in wrongdoing, a touch of humor and conscience can point the way to honest rehabilitation.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
